CRA: Default or well-known password detected
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition
account-service/src/main/java/com/piggymetrics/account/domain/User.javaLine 30
auth-service/src/main/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/domain/User.javaLine 38

auth-service/src/test/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/repository/UserRepositoryTest.javaLine 30
auth-service/src/test/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/service/UserServiceTest.javaLine 33
auth-service/src/test/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/service/UserServiceTest.javaLine 44

Explanation

EU Cyber Resilience Act (Annex I, Part I, Section 2(b)) requires a secure by default configuration. The use of default, well-known, or trivial passwords violates the secure-by-default principle.

ETSI EN 303 645 (referenced standard for CRA compliance) explicitly prohibits universal default passwords in Provision 5.1-1.

Recommended actions:

  • Remove all default/well-known passwords from code and configuration.
  • Require unique, strong passwords during initial setup.
  • Use generated secrets that are unique per deployment.
  • Implement password complexity requirements.
CRA: Hard-coded password in Java source code
 Mandatory 8
FilePosition
account-service/src/test/java/com/piggymetrics/account/controller/AccountControllerTest.javaLine 129

auth-service/src/test/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/service/UserServiceTest.javaLine 44

Explanation

EU Cyber Resilience Act (Annex I, Part I, Section 2(b)) requires products to be delivered with a secure by default configuration and to protect against unauthorized access using appropriate authentication mechanisms.

Hard-coded passwords in source code are a critical security vulnerability. They cannot be easily changed, may be exposed through version control systems, and violate the principle of secure by default.

Recommended actions:

  • Move all credentials to a secure secrets management system (e.g., Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault).
  • Use environment variables or externalized configuration for sensitive values.
  • Use connection pooling with credential providers instead of static credentials.
  • For development, use .env files that are excluded from version control.
CRA: Use of weak password hashing (plain MD5/SHA for passwords)
 Mandatory 8
FilePosition
auth-service/src/main/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/config/OAuth2AuthorizationConfig.javaLine 26
auth-service/src/main/java/com/piggymetrics/auth/config/OAuth2AuthorizationConfig.javaLine 79

Explanation

EU Cyber Resilience Act (Annex I, Part I, Section 2(b)(c)) requires robust authentication mechanisms and state of the art cryptography.

Using simple hash algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 without salt/iteration) for password storage is insecure. These hashes can be reversed using rainbow tables or brute-force attacks with modern GPUs.

Recommended actions:

  • Use bcrypt (BCryptPasswordEncoder in Spring Security).
  • Use Argon2 (Argon2PasswordEncoder in Spring Security).
  • Use PBKDF2 with at least 600,000 iterations (PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256).
  • Use scrypt (SCryptPasswordEncoder in Spring Security).
  • Ensure all password hashing uses a unique salt per password.

Explanation

The application uses a MongoDB connection string. To migrate a Java application that uses a MongoDB connection string to Azure, you can follow these recommendations:

* Use a managed Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB: Create a managed Cosmos DB for MongoDB database in Azure and choose the appropriate pricing tier based on your application's requirements for performance, storage, and availability.

* Connect to Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB using Service Connector: Create service connection using Service Connector to connect your application to Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB. Service Connector provides a secure and easy way to connect your application to Azure services without having to manage secrets or credentials in your application code.

* Passwordless connections for Azure services: Consider using passwordless connections for Azure services. You can provide an additional layer of security and convenience for accessing resources in Azure by eliminating the need for passwords. This way you can reduce the risk of password-related vulnerabilities, such as weak passwords or password theft.

Using clear passwords in property files is a security risk, as they can be easily compromised if the files are accessed by unauthorized individuals. To enhance the security of your application, it is recommended to employ secure credential management practices.

* Azure Key Vault: Utilize Azure Key Vault to securely store and manage your application's passwords and other sensitive credentials. Azure Key Vault provides a centralized and highly secure location for storing secrets, keys, and certificates.

* Passwordless connections: You can provide an additional layer of security and convenience for accessing resources in Azure by eliminating the need for passwords. This way you can reduce the risk of password-related vulnerabilities, such as weak passwords or password theft.

Explanation

The application uses Spring AMQP dependency. To migrate a Java application that uses Spring AMQP to Azure, you can follow these recommendations:

* Provision Azure Service Bus: Use Azure Service Bus, a fully managed messaging service that offers reliable message queuing and publish/subscribe capabilities.

* Update the application's messaging connection details: Modify the Java application's configuration updating the connection information and message queues/topics.

* Configure Azure Service Bus queues/topics: Create appropriate queues or topics in Azure Service Bus to align with your application's messaging requirements. Configure access control and security settings as needed.
